(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]]. ==High school career== Brown attended [[Ocean View High School]] where he averaged 14.0 points and 6.0 rebounds per game as a junior, while being named league MVP. That year he led the Seahawks to a CIF Southern Section championship and state runner-up finish and was named CIF Southern Section Player of the Year and a member of the first-team all-state. His high school jersey was retired and he was inducted into the Hall of Fame. He was the No. 7-ranked small forward, No. 41 player overall and a four-star recruit by Scout.com.{{cite web|title=Anthony Brown|url=http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208169736|publisher=Stanford|access-date=June 30, 2015}} ==College career== Brown attended Stanford from 2010 to 2015.{{cite web|first=Tom|last=FitzGerald|url=http://www.sfgate.com/collegesports/article/Experienced-Anthony-Brown-helps-Stanford-in-all-6013814.php|title=Experienced Anthony Brown helps Stanford in all phases of game|work=SFGate.com|date=January 13, 2015|access-date=January 13, 2015}}{{cite web|first=Aaron |last=Falk |url=http://www.sltrib.com/home/2626941-155/utah-jazz-stanfords-anthony-brown-shows |title=Utah Jazz: Stanford's Anthony Brown shows his smarts at pre-draft workout |work=SLTrib.com |date=June 15, 2015 |access-date=June 15, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628214429/http://www.sltrib.com/home/2626941-155/utah-jazz-stanfords-anthony-brown-shows |archive-date=June 28, 2015 }} Brown had a medical redshirt in his true junior season of 2012–13 due to a hip injury. In his redshirt junior season of 2013–14, he averaged 12.3 points and 5.0 rebounds per game and shot 47.5% from the floor, 45.3% from beyond the arc and 78.5% on free throws. He was named the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]]'s Most Improved Player as the Cardinal reached the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Tournament.{{cite news|last1=Johnson|first1=Raphielle|title=Stanford guard Anthony Brown looks to take another step forward in 2014–15|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/07/20/stanford-guard-anthony-brown-looks-to-take-another-step-forward-in-2014-15/|access-date=June 25, 2015|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=July 20, 2014}} As a senior Brown led Stanford to the NIT championship while averaging 14.8 points (10th in the Pac-12), a team-high 6.9 rebounds (8th), and 2.5 assists per game. He had the eighth best free-throw percentage in the Pac-12, at 79.4 per cent.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/anthony-brown-5.html|title=Anthony Brown College Stats|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}} During his career he averaged 10.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game. Brown completed his bachelor's degree in communication in May 2014 and was enrolled in Stanford's [[Master of Arts]] program in media studies in his redshirt senior season.{{cite web|title=Senior Night vs. Oregon |url=http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30600&ATCLID=209915694 |publisher=Stanford Athletics |access-date=June 30, 2015 |date=February 28, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150802000353/http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30600 |archive-date=August 2, 2015 }} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Lakers (2015–2016)=== On June 25, 2015, Brown was selected with the 34th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/150625_browndraft|title=Lakers Take Anthony Brown With 34th Pick|work=NBA.com|date=June 25, 2015|access-date=June 27, 2015}} On July 9, he signed with the Lakers.{{cite news|title=Lakers Sign Anthony Brown|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/150709_anthonyBrown|access-date=July 9, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015}} He made his debut for the Lakers on October 30, scoring five points off the bench in a loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151030/LALSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Rondo, Cousins lead Kings to 132–114 win over Lakers|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2015|access-date=October 31, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160123231011/http://www.nba.com/games/20151030/LALSAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 23, 2016|url-status=dead}} During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments to the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]], the Lakers' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2015–16 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160624025744/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/ |archive-date=June 24, 2016 }} On October 24, 2016, he was waived by the Lakers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/161024-anthony-brown|title=Lakers Waive Anthony Brown|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016}} ===Erie BayHawks and NBA stints (2016–2017)=== On October 30, 2016, Brown was selected by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] with the first overall pick in the 2016 NBA Development League Draft.{{cite web|url=http://erie.dleague.nba.com/news/anthonybrown/|title=BayHawks Draft Anthony Brown First Overall|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2016|access-date=October 31, 2016}} After averaging 29.3 points, 4.3 rebounds and 4.3 assists in three games, Brown signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on November 21.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-anthony-brown|title=Pelicans Sign Anthony Brown|work=NBA.com|date=November 21, 2016|access-date=November 21, 2016}} On December 9, he was waived by the Pelicans. In nine games, he averaged 3.9 points and 2.5 rebounds in 15.9 minutes.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-anthony-brown|title=Pelicans Waive Anthony Brown|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2016|access-date=December 9, 2016}} Three days later, he returned to Erie.{{cite web|first=Iris|last=Rayburn|url=http://erie.dleague.nba.com/news/anthony-brown-returns-bayhawks/|title=Anthony Brown Returns to BayHawks|work=NBA.com|date=December 12, 2016|access-date=December 12, 2016}} On January 22, 2017, Brown signed a 10-day contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-anthony-brown-10-day-contract|title=Magic Sign Anthony Brown to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 22, 2017|access-date=January 21, 2017}} On February 2, 2017, after the 10-day contract expired, Brown returned to the BayHawks.{{cite web|url=http://erie.dleague.nba.com/news/anthony-brown-returns-bayhawks-2/|title=Anthony Brown Returns to BayHawks|work=NBA.com|date=February 2, 2017|access-date=February 4, 2017}} Four days later, he was named in the Eastern Conference All-Star team for the 2017 NBA D-League All-Star Game.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2017-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|title=Rosters for 2017 NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented By Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2017|access-date=February 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207120954/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2017-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|archive-date=February 7, 2017|url-status=dead}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves/Iowa Wolves (2017–2018)=== On August 1, 2017, Brown was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Under the terms of the deal, he will split time between the Timberwolves and their G-League affiliate, the [[Iowa Wolves]]. He became the first player in franchise history to sign a two-way contract.{{cite news|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN ANTHONY BROWN TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-anthony-brown-two-way-contract|access-date=August 1, 2017|work=[[Minnesota Timberwolves]]|date=August 1, 2017}} On August 29, 2018, Brown signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on a training camp contract.{{cite web|title=Team Signs Anthony Brown|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/team-signs-anthony-brown|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 29, 2018|date=August 29, 2018}} On October 10, 2018, Brown was waived by the 76ers.{{cite web|title=In corresponding moves, the team has waived Anthony Brown and Norvel Pelle.|url=https://twitter.com/sixers/status/1050133250973286406|date=October 10, 2018|website=Philadelphia 76ers on Twitter|access-date=October 10, 2018}} ===Partizan (2018)=== On October 23, 2018, Brown signed with Serbian club [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] for the rest of the 2018–19 season.{{cite web|title=Anthony Brown in Partizan NIS|url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=40786|date=October 23, 2018|website=aba-liga.com|access-date=October 23, 2018}} On November 27, 2018, he parted ways with Partizan.{{Cite news|url=http://kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest/2404/entoni-braun-vise-nije-igrac-partizana-nis|title=Entoni Braun više nije igrač Partizana NIS|newspaper=Normacore.com |last1=Normasoft.
